pageCache.text:
I am an Ursuline Today, tomorrow, always
Welcome
Headteacher, Mark O'Shaughnessy
The school was established in 1877 by the Ursuline Order and continues to have as its inspiration the spirit and traditions of the congregation.
As an Ursuline school, we have been entrusted by St Angela, our foundress, to continue to live out her vision of educating young women of tomorrow. Our school motto is “Serviam” meaning “I shall serve.” We are a testament to this in that our school community bears witness to God’s love; whereby each individual is encouraged to serve and love one another.
See our latest Ofsted inspection here.
Catholic Values
St Ursula’s is a part of a global network of schools with an Ursuline tradition and charism. The Ursuline Education Community was established in 2019 with the main aim to unite all the Ursuline schools in the UK.
The Ursuline Education Community produced an ‘Ursuline Pupil Profile’ that aims to describe the whole process of Ursuline education rather than that of a school leaver. The virtues are displayed in every classroom and our daily prayer and reflections and assemblies all focus on the virtue of the term.

pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
SERVIAM: WORKING TOGETHER WITH RESPECT FOR ALL
SERVIAM is the motto of all Ursuline schools worldwide. The word Serviam is Latin for “I will serve”. It is inspired by the teachings of St Angela Merici, Foundress of the Ursuline Order.
Serviam is at the heart of every student at St. Ursula’s Convent School and for many, the importance of Serviam stays with them long after they have left the school.
As well as taking part in an activity, students reflect on how this activity has helped them to understand, develop or deepen the virtue they are focusing on. By reflecting on how students are developing their virtues, students are contributing to their own character development and recognising the true happiness (eudaimonia) that comes from being of service to others.
All students participate in the wider life of the school to develop their gifts and talents as well contribute to the Common Good.
Students’ contribution to the ethos of the school and development of Serviam is recognised and celebrated regularly in school with a termly certificate for those selected by any member of staff.
Our schools core values are those around the tree:
Just a few acts of Serviam that some students may get involved in at St. Ursula’s Convent School:
United in harmony
Generous & grateful
Listening &attentive
Loving & compassionate
Faith-filled & Hopeful
Courageous & resilient
Discerning & joyful
Leading for justice
Acting with truth & integrity
Helping in the community
Harvest festivals collections for food banks

Welcome to St Ursula's Convent School
Dear Students, Parents and Carers,
I am delighted to be able to welcome you to the website of St Ursula’s Convent School for Girls. I am privileged to be Headteacher at St Ursula’s, leading the school with the support of the Senior Leadership Team and Governing Body.
Having grown up in South East London I have always been aware of St Ursula’s and in taking up this role as very mindful of the mission of the school:
Our motto of Serviam means that through our daily lives we will seek to discover, nourish, cherish, and develop the talents of all the students at the school. We believe that everyone has unique talents and believe it is the mission of the school to help our young people discover theirs.
Although I have only been at St Ursula’s a short time there is an unmistakable identity to the school, both the environment and the atmosphere. A Saint Ursula’s student is one who has high aspirations, who values community and respects others.
Central to our school is our Catholic faith. As a Catholic school every girl is valued for their uniqueness and individuality, and as an inclusive school we welcome girls of all faiths and of none. All of our students will be individually known and valued.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Ursula's Convent School - About Us
pageCache.text:
History of St Ursula's Convent School
The Ursuline convent at Greenwich was founded from Duderstadt in Germany on 1 October 1877. The sisters had lived in Duderstadt since 1700 but they were expelled from their convent by the German Chancellor Bismarck who wanted the state to control all educational establishments.
After some searching the sisters found a suitable property, 70 Crooms Hill, Greenwich, formerly a boys’ orphanage but subsequently empty. They took the house on a 50 year lease at £80 a year and 21 sisters came over from Duderstadt, opening their first school with 25 pupils.
Five years later, however, in 1882, an appeal came from an Australian bishop for the sisters to make a foundation in New South Wales, ‘Ten sisters volunteered to go, and after a journey of more than 3 months they reached Armidale and set up a school, eventually establishing a network of convents across the state and up into Queensland.
Meanwhile in Greenwich the school was proving popular and in 1886 the sisters purchased St Mary’s Lodge, adjoining 70 Crooms Hill and doubling the size of the property with its generous accommodation and garden. At this point however, circumstances in Germany were improving and 12 of the 15 sisters left at Greenwich were anxious to return home.
At the same time the French government had, it its turn, become very anti-Catholic, and was moving towards legislation to close all convents and take over their schools, so the Ursuline sisters of Gravelines in N. France were looking for an alternative refuge. In 1892 therefore the German sisters at Greenwich asked if they would be interested in taking over their school in England. The convent on Crooms Hill was so attractively situated that the French Ursulines readily agreed to continue the work the German sisters had started.
The school now had French boarders, as well as German, Norwegian and English students, and the boarding school remained in existence until 1950. But increasingly the concentration was on day pupils and on building up academic subjects. St Ursula’s was officially recognised as a small private school in 1904. In 1920 it was able to admit scholarship pupils and by 1935 it was an efficient 2-form entry grammar school.
Then in 1939 came World War 2. The school was evacuated to Hastings and when this became too dangerous they moved to Brecon in South Wales. Eventually peace returned, and when the school became Voluntary Aided in 1949 fee-paying ceased and numbers began to build. In 1977 in yet another development St Ursula’s became a 3-form entry comprehensive school.
The Sixth Form expanding to 100 had their own specialised accommodation in Heathgate and Stobcross. In time however sixth form opportunities needed to offer a wider choice, and St Ursula’s opted to support the new sixth form college structure which was emerging. As a consequence the school became 11-16 and 4-form entry. This has allowed for greater choice and variety in the curriculum, and the school is held in such high esteem that applications to enter the school each year number 4 times its actual capacity to accept them.
In 1992 the sisters moved out of St Mary’s Lodge which had been the convent for 110 years and this area was given over to the expanding school. The present convent is now to be found in Heathgate and Stobcross, formerly the sixth form area. There the sisters continue to pray for the wellbeing of everyone connected with St Ursula’s – both past and present.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Ursula's Convent School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Here at St Ursuline's, we are an Ursuline school founded by the Ursuline Sisters. Our moto is SERVIAM which means ‘ I will serve’. As an Ursuline community we do our utmost to live this put each day in our school, local community and the wider world by putting our faith into action.
We have a full-time chaplain to serve the needs of the community, staff and students, and to develop the prayer life and Ursuline charism of the school. We also have year 11 Chaplaincy prefects and a Chaplaincy team in each year group who work with the Chaplain to support the spiritual and pastoral life of students and their families. The Chaplain also works to support the staff in their work with students and to encourage students in their own spiritual development.
Each morning in registration students take part in a form of collective worship, whether this be in assembly or in their form groups following the structure below. Each day students are asked to lead and take part and once a week it is planned and led by the students.
Each lesson at St Ursula’s begins with our school prayer and each day in collective worship we say the prayer of St Angela
We offer you this lesson for your greater honour and glory.
Holy Guardian Angel watch over us.
St. Ursula pray for us.
Sacrament of Reconciliation
During Advent and Lent, all pupils and staff are given the opportunity to receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation.
Each Friday students and staff are invited to attend 8am Mass at our parish church Our Ladye Star of the Sea, led by Fr Kevin our parish priest. It is a wonderful opportunity to gather as a school community in God’s presence.
St Ursula’s as an Ursuline School has strong links to the worldwide network of Ursuline Schools. We regularly link with other local and international Ursuline Schools sharing our faith, learning and experiences.
Sr Kathleen the Ursuline provincial comes in once a month to run Ursuline links with year 11. This group is all about living out SERVIAM and so far this year they have held a collection for the local food bank and written Christmas cards to give out at a local care home.

pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
Welcome to the MFL Department
Our MFL curriculum celebrates linguistic and cultural diversity, encouraging students to develop understanding, empathy, and a sense of appreciation for others.
Our curriculum is both academically rigorous and accessible, remaining flexible and responsive to the latest research and recommendations from recognised best practices.
We believe every student, regardless of background or ability, has the capacity and right to learn another language. We are committed to removing barriers to success, providing tailored support, and fostering an inclusive environment where all students thrive. Our aim is to equip every learner with valuable linguistic skills that enhance their academic and personal lives.
We offer French and Spanish. Through the study of these languages, students develop independent learning skills that are transferable to other disciplines, ensuring that the tools acquired in language learning contribute to success across the curriculum, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and adaptability.
Our curriculum equips students with the metacognitive skills necessary for lifelong learning. By understanding the processes of language acquisition, students are empowered to continue their intellectual journey beyond school, for personal, professional, or spiritual enrichment.

These three key elements are reinforced through spaced repetition, sufficiency, and retrieval practice to ensure mastery and long-term retention.
At St. Ursula’s Convent School, we view language learning as a transformative journey—a discovery of diverse cultures, the world, and universal love. Guided by the Ursuline motto, Serviam, we are committed to nurturing students to grow in knowledge and readiness to contribute positively to our modern, interconnected global community.
Head of Modern Foreign Languages

pageCache.pageTitle: St Ursula's Convent School - Computer Science
pageCache.text:
Computer Science
Welcome to the Computer Science Department
In the Computer Science Department, we believe in a creative and collaborative approach to exploring computing while developing problem-solving and computational thinking skills.
We have two members of staff in the Computer Science Department, we are both very passionate about ensuring the students have every opportunity to develop their programming skills. We understand the importance of Computer science and developing the student's skills to be confident Digital Leaders and prepare students for jobs that do not yet exist and to use technology that has not yet been invented.
We have an ambitious Curriculum which explores machine learning algorithms and allows students to create computer games and programming AI Models. We aim to ensure every pupil can develop their Computing and Digital skills not only in the classroom but also in gaining opportunities outside of the classroom. This year we are taking the students on a Trip to Euro Disney to understand how technology is used in the Leisure industry.
The Computer Science department puts students’ projects and ideas at the heart of the department. We have close links with Morgan Stanley who run a coding club every week with our KS4 students.
We encourage and support students to pursue their own interests. This has seen the development of the Robotics Club with students gearing up to take part in the Lego League Competition.

KS4/KS3 Ms Remy Assistant Headteacher

Drama
Welcome to the Drama Department
Drama at St Ursula’s is about far more than performance—it is about imagination, confidence and collaboration. Through our curriculum, students learn to devise, perform and evaluate drama, while also developing communication and teamwork skills that will benefit them in all areas of life.
We extend learning beyond the classroom with drama clubs, trips to live theatre and workshops with professionals from the creative industries. Students also have the chance to explore behind-the-scenes roles such as set and costume design, stage management, lighting and sound.
Drama is at the heart of school life, with regular showcases, our annual Passion Play and whole-school productions bringing students together to create inspiring performances. Every child has the opportunity to shine—whether on stage or as part of the creative team—and to discover the power of storytelling through theatre.
Director of Performing Arts
drama learning journey pptx.pdf

Music
Welcome to the Music Department
At St Ursula’s, music plays a vital role in helping our young people grow in confidence, creativity and self-expression. Our curriculum gives students the chance to perform, compose and explore a wide variety of musical styles, building both technical skills and a lifelong love of music.
We offer a rich programme of enrichment opportunities, including choir, school rock and pop bands, and instrumental ensembles. Students can also take peripatetic lessons in guitar, piano, drums, violin and voice, allowing them to develop their talents further.
Music is celebrated across the school through regular showcases and performances, as well as our much-anticipated annual musical. Whether on stage, behind the scenes, or in the audience, every child has the chance to experience the joy of live performance and be part of our vibrant musical community.
Director of Performing Arts

pageCache.pageTitle: St Ursula's Convent School - GCSE Results 2026
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results 2026
GCSE Results Day 2026
On the 19th August 2026, our 2025/2026 Year 11 students returned to school to collect their GCSE grades. Results were strong across the board, but some individual subject areas shone, with the English Department achieving 89% at grade 4 or higher, the Computer Science Department achieving 83% at grade 4 or higher, Maths achieving 75% at grade 4 or higher, and Religious Education achieving 80% at grade 4 or higher.
A number of departments also gained excellent grades at the highest levels, such as English with 37% achieving grades 7–9, French with 64% achieving grades 7–9, Chemistry and Physics with 50% achieving grades 7–9, and History with 41% achieving grades 7–9.
“We are incredibly proud of our students and everything they have achieved. Today’s results are a wonderful celebration of our students’ dedication, success and support for one another. This year’s results demonstrate a clear improvement in the progress students are making from their individual starting points. Compared with previous years, students have made stronger progress throughout their time at the school, reflecting the impact of high-quality teaching, targeted academic support and the commitment shown by both students and staff. This represents an important step forward for the school and provides a strong foundation on which to build in the years ahead.”
- Mr O'Shaughnessy, Headteacher.
See our amazing results published in Independent Catholic News here - https://www.indcatholicnews.com/news/55708

Parents
We extend a warm welcome to all parents and carers. We are committed to creating an atmosphere where every student feels valued, supported, and encouraged to achieve their full potential.
As a result, we encourage you to actively engage with our SCHOOL community by attending our Parent Focus Group or joining the Friends of St Ursula’s, a group of volunteers who work on projects to enhance the experience for everyone at the school. We value your involvement as it plays a crucial role in your child’s academic and lifelong journey.
Edulink One – to contact parents/carers
The school uses of Edu Link One to increase the quality of information to parents and continue our commitment to paperless systems by reducing workload, reducing costs and increasing time for our core purpose of teaching and learning. Therefore, we will deliver all reports and communication to parents and carers while using the app and website. EduLink One uses live data from SIMS with the potential to complete registers quickly, create seating plans, view or add progress, achievement or behaviour data, set detentions, communicate with parents, book resources such as Chromebooks and much more.
https://www.edulinkone.com/#!/login
If you have any questions, concerns, or suggestions, please do not hesitate to reach out to us at admin@stursulas.com to support you and your child in every way we can.
We look forward to a rewarding partnership with you and your family this year and beyond.
